why: The whole of issue #428, put back. A page that has shown nobody anything owns a canvas, a renderer, a GL context, a simulation world, a gameplay seed and a frame loop again, and a player who opens the game and walks away pays for a match they never asked for. 41 of 66 in the scoped run, and the breadth is the point rather than a nuisance: the eager start is not one behaviour but the premise every session-shaped assertion in boot.test.ts used to rest on, so re-adding it breaks the empty-boot counts, every start-gesture count (each reads one session too many), and the whole reboot ledger. The narrow half is 'reaches the application UI with no session, no canvas and no world', which is the one that would fail even if every other case were rewritten around it. COUNT RE-MEASURED for issue #429 on the final tree: main's 34 of 58 -> 41 of 66. boot.test.ts gains the eight-test return-to-routes suite, and seven of those eight fail under an eager start; the eighth asserts only that the page owners survive, which the mutation does not touch. The failing set was decomposed, not renumbered: 34 of the 41 name tests that exist unchanged on main, and 7 are the new suite's. main declares 34, so the pre-existing count is unchanged; individual pre-existing verdicts were not re-measured on main's tree. An earlier 39 recorded on this branch matched no tree it shipped on -- CI and a local re-run both measure 41.
